South Africa's Economic Funk

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the country's economy plunges into turbulent waters is there a lifeline to save it

Unique Selling Point:
South Africa's economy is facing a looming crisis. As things stand,the GDP is shrinking, government debt is staggering, SOEs are broke and broken and in November we face a credit downgrade which will put the country in junk status. Bringing together voices from business, government economic sector, the presidency and investors, the insert will look at how we can possibly fix the economy and dodge serious meltdown.

Summary:
Busisiwe Mavuso from BLSA will speak about how South African businesses have been affected by the economic downturn and how they believe the situation can be turned around. Business confidence in the economy and government has dropped and to continue operating and growing business is having to traverse difficult waters.

Dr Thabi Leokoa, economic analyst will put in simple terms things like ratings downgrade, IMF bailout, recession and what these mean for the ordinary citizen. She will also analyse and rate how Finance Minister Tito Mboweni is steering S.A's economic ship out of crisis.

Leon Ayo - is president of British BUsiness Chambers in South Africa, he will talk about how investors view the situation the country finds itself in, if South Africa is still an attractive investor destination.

Phumzile Langeni was appointed as an envoy to attract investment into the country. She's travelled to various countries around the world selling South Africa to potential investors - she will speak about how her role and the plan to turn to attract investment into the country when things are dire.

Tito Mboweni - Finance Minister has the very difficult job of trying to come with a strategy to grow the country's economy when all the odds are laid out against him. Nonetheless as the person responsible for the country's economic purse he needs to show leadership and be innovative. His interview will unpack how he plans to do this.

S.A Economic Funk Script Visuals
VO/LINK Upsound inner city trading/poverty viz money in hands Spar

Link/VO: The effects of South Africa’s consistent economic decline have been devastating. You’ve seen it in the unemployment figures and rising poverty and felt it where it hurts the most – your pocket.

VO: For Economist- Dr Thabi Leoka – the country is in a very critical state
VO: It hasn’t always been like this – prior to the 2008 financial crisis – our economy was registering good growth, we had manageable debt and an impressive investment track record. Masa Question 01:28 “ Thabi if you were to describe South Africa’s economy right now – what words would you use” Thabi 01:34 “I'd say the South African economy is in ICU and needs to be resuscitated and there hasn’t been much effort to resuscitate it…

Masa – ICU that not only sounds critical but serious and dangerous
Thabi “ VO: However since then - South Africa’s economy has struggled to find its footing…

VO: Dr Montfort Mlachila – Is the International Monetary Fund Senior Representative in South Africa. The IMF is a global organisation that monitors economic and financial developments around the world. It also lends money to countries facing financial constraints.

VO:He says the country’s economic growth has been too low for too long. Montfort Mlachila 10:47 – 10:57 “since the global financial crisis there’s been some divergence - in other words South African economy has been going down while the rest of its peers have actually recovered.” Montfort Mlachila 00:53 – 01:04 “the economic growth in South Africa has been about 1 percent over the past few years and clearly that’s very low” 04:23 “ that’s rather unusual for a country that’s not facing a civil war or some political turmoil Visuals of street vendors Visuals of guys selling stuff on the streets/to cars
**VO: But South Africa is not in a civil war Monty 02:17 “But truly what is a cause for concern for us is that the pace of economic reforms to address the challenges that the country is facing have not been not been up to the expected levels” Monty - the government can undertake a number of measures that are relatively straightforward and have relatively high pay offs - for example facilitating the issuance of visas for example especially for tourists and as well as for highly skilled workers. And thirdly there would be a need to address the very weak finances of the state owned enterprises which are a drain on the fiscus.

SOE LINK SABC/ESKOM Tito Mboweni Upsound 19:59 – 20:47 “The SOEs poses a very serious risk to the fiscal framework - isn’t it about time that the country asks itself the question - do we still need all these enterprises - if we do -can we manage them better?” Thabi “How I always explain it is Eskom’s debt is equivalent to South Africa’s sovereign debt before 2008” VO: Not only is our debt putting a strain on our fiscus - it is also putting a stain on our credit rating - in other words our credit score. This means investors think twice about putting money into South Africa..

Credit Rating Link Masa Question: What does junk status mean to an ordinary South African…. Thabi: “I like the word junk because the formal word is sub-investment - but junk everybody understands it’s trash and belongs to the bin. And for countries that are mandated to invest in investment grade countries - they would have to pull out- the rand would weaken”…..

JSE LINK VO: Leon Ayo - is the President of the British Chamber of BUsiness in South Africa.
VO:He says, he remains enthusiastic about bringing Business into the country, and that investors are now starting to sow - in tech driven industries Leon “....” Leon “...” Ramaphosa- In Parliament 4:43 - 5:45

VO: whilst the president has emphasised that growing the economy is his top priority - in the meantime what options does government have to channel money into the fiscus.

**VO: The government presented a plan of action to reignite economic growth - This is the Stimulus Package released in 2018. However Dr Mlachila cautions that investors will only buy into it once they see it being implemented... Masa Question - We keep hearing about IMF bailout- will we go that route Thabi “ I don’t think so Masa Question - In Octobe MOnty 20:31 Investors actually do require more than potential - they do care about policy certainty – they do care that the rules of the game are gonna be predictable and will be observed by everyone. So by undertaking a lot of these reforms to assure investors that’s the only way you can unlock potential.

VO: As the country anticipates what could be a big blow in November - Leon Ayo says in the global context South Africa’s economic woes are not particularly unique to us. Leon Ayo “
